Summarise environmental values around observations

Source: R/extract_to_buffer.R
extract_to_buffer.Rd

Calculates one statistic per observation from the values in a buffer around it: a circle of horizontal_radius_km, a depth window of depth_radius_m above and below the observation, and a time window from time_before to time_after. It is a convenience wrapper over the three steps of an analysis, and the workflow article shows the same steps written out:

Usage

extract_to_buffer(
  data,
  nc,
  var = NULL,
  horizontal_radius_km = 0,
  depth_radius_m = 0,
  time_before = 0,
  time_after = 0,
  time_unit = c("days", "hours", "minutes", "seconds"),
  statistic = c("mean", "sd", "min", "max"),
  weighting = c("weighted", "equal"),
  method = NULL,
  lon_col = "lon",
  lat_col = "lat",
  depth_col = "depth",
  date_col = "date",
  lon_dim = NULL,
  lat_dim = NULL,
  depth_dim = NULL,
  time_dim = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  output_col = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Observation table, matrix, named list or sf POINT object.

nc

The data: a netCDF file path, several paths for a series of files on one grid, an open ncdf4::nc_open() connection, a SpatProxy from as_proxy(), or a SpatVoxel in memory.

var

Name of the variable, for a netCDF source. NULL detects the only data variable of the file.

horizontal_radius_km

Radius of the circle around each observation, in kilometres, measured on the WGS84 ellipsoid, below 10000 as in buffer_3d(). 0 (default) uses the observation's own cell.

depth_radius_m

Distance in metres above and below the observation's depth. 0 (default) picks one level per cell with method.

time_before, time_after

Time before and after the observation, in time_unit. Both 0 (default) read the one time step time_match matches. For observations with dates and no hours, the window covers whole UTC days, including the last.

time_unit

"days" (default), "hours", "minutes" or "seconds".

statistic

One of "mean" (default), "sd", "min" and "max".

weighting

"weighted" (default) weights each value by the volume of its cell and level with a depth window, and by its cell's area without one (one level per cell) or for a variable without depth; "equal" counts each value once.

method

How the level in each cell is chosen when there is no depth window: one of the rules of mask() for points, "nearest" (default; the level nearest the observation's depth that has a value), "nearest_level" (the nearest level, even if it has no value), "bottom" or "surface". Leave NULL with a depth window. For a variable without depth, leave NULL or use "2d".

lon_col, lat_col, depth_col, date_col

Observation columns. The depth is needed with a depth window or a "nearest" rule, and the date for data with several time steps. Dates and date-times are read as in as_vector3d().

lon_dim, lat_dim, depth_dim, time_dim

Dimension names for a netCDF source, as in as_proxy().

time_match, max_time_diff

Without a time window, how the time step is matched, as in as_voxel(): the nearest step (default) or an exact one, and the largest gap in days for a nearest match.

output_col

Name of the output column. NULL uses the variable's name.

Value

data with two columns added: the statistic, named output_col or after the variable, and <output>_n, the number of values it is built on. sf input keeps its geometry. If data already has either column, the function stops with an error; choose another output_col.

Details

  1. Build: each observation becomes a point with as_vector3d(), and a buffer with buffer_3d() when horizontal_radius_km is positive.

  2. Intersect: the data for its time steps are read with crop() and as_voxel() (or rast() for a variable without depth), and the values inside the buffer are kept with mask().

  3. Summarise: summarise_3d() gives the statistic of those values.

A cell or depth level counts in full when the buffer reaches it, as in mask(): a cell the circle touches, and a level whose slab of water overlaps the depth window. With weighting = "weighted" each value is weighted by the volume of its cell and level (by the cell's area for a variable without depth, or when method picks one level per cell), as summarise_3d() does.

Without a depth window, method picks the level in each cell: by default the level nearest the observation's depth that has a value, as extract_to_point() does. Without a radius, the buffer is the observation's own cell. Without a time window, the time step is the one time_match matches. A time window pools the values of every time step inside it into one statistic, each value keeping its own weight.

An observation outside the grid, without a date on data with several time steps, without a depth where one is needed (or with a negative one), or with no time step in its window or within max_time_diff gets NA, and <output>_n is 0. One warning counts these observations, by reason. On data with several time steps on one day, observations need date-times or a time window: a date alone can't pick one of the steps, so the function stops.

See also

extract_to_point(), extract_to_area(), and the workflow article.

Examples

# Daily temperature on a 10 x 10 grid of 1 degree cells at four depths.
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".nc")
lon <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("lon", "degrees_east", seq(0.5, 9.5))
lat <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("lat", "degrees_north", seq(0.5, 9.5))
depth <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("depth", "m", c(5, 15, 30, 60))
time <- ncdf4::ncdim_def("time", "days since 2020-01-01", 0:2)
temp <- ncdf4::ncvar_def("temp", "degree_Celsius",
                         list(lon, lat, depth, time), -9999)
nc <- ncdf4::nc_create(path, temp)
ncdf4::ncvar_put(nc, temp, seq_len(10 * 10 * 4 * 3) / 10)
ncdf4::nc_close(nc)

obs <- data.frame(lon = 5.2, lat = 5.3, depth = 20,
                  date = as.Date("2020-01-02"))

# The mean within 150 km and 10 m above and below, on the observation's day.
extract_to_buffer(obs, path, horizontal_radius_km = 150,
                  depth_radius_m = 10)
#>   lon lat depth       date     temp temp_n
#> 1 5.2 5.3    20 2020-01-02 61.60395     26

# Pooled over a day either side.
extract_to_buffer(obs, path, horizontal_radius_km = 150,
                  depth_radius_m = 10, time_before = 1, time_after = 1)
#>   lon lat depth       date     temp temp_n
#> 1 5.2 5.3    20 2020-01-02 61.60395     78
